text:
anya: heads-up — found a reproducible shortening of katakana lines with ellipses when running the int4 onboard build on the subtitle corpus.
shawn: can you paste a tiny repro? curious if it's tokenizer or runtime. :thinking_face:
anya: quick sample: fp16 -> "彼は… 死んだ"  (keeps the ellipsis token). int4 -> "彼は 死んだ" (ellip removed, next token shifts).
mei: omg that shift could break alignment with en subs. do you have token ids?
anya: yes — took a single step decode snapshot: \n```\n# fp16 tokens\n[1012, 5543, 823, 9999]  # 5543 = '彼', 823 = 'は', 9999 = '…'\n# int4 tokens\n[1012, 5543, 823]  # ellipsis missing\n```\nhiro: curious if it's the tokenizer merging `...` -> `…` in preproc then quant kernel dropping the single-byte token. did you try forcing byte-level tokenization?
anya: forced tokenizer raw mode showed the `…` token exists in vocab. When we run `--quantize=int4 --fast-kernel` the token disappears.
shawn: suspicious of KV-cache indexing / stride when a single-token prefix is removed. could be an address calc bug in the int4 path.
mei: any diffs in logits before sampling? even small -inf could zero out token.
anya: logged topk logits for the position: fp16 top tokens: `[(9999, -1.2), (4321, -3.5)]` int4 top tokens: `[(4321, -0.1), (1012, -2.9)]` — ellipsis dropped from top.
hiro: hmm that smells like quant rounding pushing 9999's logit below threshold. is calibration using same dataset?
anya: used default minmax per-tensor calibration from our int4 flow. trying per-channel next.
mei: can you run a small bisect? try disabling int4 fast-kernel (fallback to reference) and see if the token returns.
anya: done — when fallback to ref kernel, ellipsis stays. enabling fast-kernel reproduces drop.
shawn: can you run a micro-benchmark comparing `compute_top_logits` between kernels with the same inputs? even printing raw fp32 logits before quantization would help.
eval-bot: perf/run/2398769999 completed — artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/2398769999/{logits.npy,token_traces.json}
anya: uploading a short repro gist and the small model shard to s3; link in thread. next steps: (1) kernel owners to review rounding code path, (2) try per-channel calibration, (3) check tokenizer edge-case for multiple dots -> U+2026 mapping.
hiro: I'll take kernel owner action. assigning to @shawn for bisect and @mei to run per-channel cal quickly.
shawn: will bisect tomorrow morning PST. thanks for clear repro, anya. :pray:
mei: running per-channel now, will post results in thread.
anya: thanks — this one is probably subtle but high impact for subtitles and short-turn dialogs.
notes: short thread, reproducer + logs attached; follow-up actions assigned
